comparisons.peer_summary: Client operating income improved to an $897 million profit in 2024 from a $46 million operating loss in 2023, primarily due to higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD report significant improvements in segment operating income for fiscal 2024. MU attributes its CNBU operating income improvement to higher bit shipments, increased average selling prices (ASPs), and cost reductions. Similarly, AMD reports that its Client segment operating income improved to a profit, primarily due to higher revenue, though it was partially offset by higher operating expenses. Both companies experienced positive operating income shifts driven by revenue growth factors, though MU specifically highlights cost reductions and ASP increases as drivers, while AMD highlights the transition from a loss to a profit in its Client segment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose substantial growth in their respective Data Center-focused segments, driven by specific high-demand products. MU's CNBU operating income improved due to higher bit shipments and ASPs, while AMD's Data Center operating income rose to $3.5 billion, primarily due to higher revenue driven by AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. Both companies benefited from strong demand in the data center/AI infrastructure space, with MU leveraging memory/bit shipments and AMD leveraging GPU/CPU sales.

comparisons.peer_summary: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023, driven by higher server revenue from high core count products, which increased average selling prices but lowered volume compared to 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC discuss the impact of Average Selling Prices (ASPs) on their revenue and operating performance. MU notes that increased ASPs were a positive driver for CNBU operating income improvement. In contrast, INTC's DCAI segment saw its revenue increase driven by higher ASPs from high core count products, but this was accompanied by lower volume. Both disclosures highlight ASP dynamics as a key variable in their respective data center/server revenue streams, though the outcomes (positive for MU, mixed with volume declines for INTC) differ.
